Microsoft Research Cambridge UK invites applications for three open research positions in our People-Centric AI research area. These roles offer the opportunity to join an interdisciplinary team working at the forefront of human-AI interaction and generative interfaces, in support of experiences that enable human agency and skill, support creativity and collaboration, and ensure equitable representation and participation.

Open positions:

**Resident (Postdoctoral) Researcher - Generative Experiences & Collaborative Workflows**

This 2-year position will focus on developing tools that use AI models to generate dynamic or malleable user experiences, where content is generated to fit the needs of end-users, or is co-created and co-evolves with their input. Candidates must have completed or be on track to a PhD in a relevant field (e.g. HCI, ML, Computer Science) or have equivalent industry experience, alongside expertise in researching and developing tools for interactions between generative AI-models and end-users.

**Intern - Generative Experiences**

This 12-week internship is a collaboration between Microsoft Research Cambridge and the OneDrive and SharePoint (ODSP) Applied Science team, bringing together research and product perspectives to explore new forms of dynamic content and generative user experiences that adapt to individual users’ context, roles, and preferences.

**Intern - Ethical and Social Implications of Provenance Disclosure**

This 12-week internship aims to address the social and ethical implications of providing provenance information for digital content. The intern will carry out research to gain a deeper understanding of the impact of revealing information like origin, creator identity, timeline of modifications, and tools used for different kinds of communities of consumers, creators and publishers.

All positions are expected to start by end of June 2026.

For more information about the People-Centric AI research area, please see our webpage: People-Centric AI - Microsoft Research<

>

Siân Lindley Co-lead of People-Centric AI Microsoft Research Cambridge UK

Microsoft is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to age, ancestry, citizenship, color, family or medical care leave, gender identity or expression, genetic information, immigration status, marital status, medical condition, national origin, physical or mental disability, political affiliation, protected veteran or military status, race, ethnicity, religion, sex (including pregnancy), sexual orientation, or any other characteristic protected by applicable local laws, regulations and ordinances.
